3. ## **Project Overview**

   1. Smart power management system using 12V DC input  
   2. Integrated 2S battery charging and backup system  
   3. Automatic power path management  
   4. Buck and boost regulated outputs  
   5. MCU-based monitoring and control  
   6. I2C communication support  
   7. Designed for uninterrupted embedded power applications

4. ## **Design Goal**

   1. Provide uninterrupted power supply operation  
   2. Support automatic battery backup switching  
   3. Implement safe battery charging  
   4. Generate stable regulated voltage rails  
   5. Reduce power loss using ideal diode architecture  
   6. Enable intelligent system monitoring  
   7. Ensure thermal and EMI reliability  
   8. Create compact and manufacturable PCB design

5. ## **Electronics Hardware Requirement**

   1. **Input Stage**  
      1. 220–240VAC SMPS  
      2. 12V DC output  
   2. **Protection Stage**  
      1. [SMBJ12CA](https://yageogroup.com/content/datasheet/asset/file/SMBJ-AT_1) TVS diode  
      2. [LM73100](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm7310.pdf) ideal diode controller  
   3. **Battery Management**  
      1. [MP2760](https://www.monolithicpower.com/en/documentview/productdocument/index/version/2/document_type/Datasheet/lang/en/sku/MP2760GVT/document_id/9800/) battery charger and power path controller  
      2.  6 pin JST Connector for 2S SES battery charging  
   4. **MCU Power Supply**  
      1. [LMR54410](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lmr54406.pdf) buck converter  
      2. 3.3V regulated output  
   5. **Load Switching**  
      1. [DMP4006SPSWQ P](https://www.diodes.com/assets/Datasheets/DMP4006SPSWQ.pdf)\-MOSFET  
      2. [LTC2955-2](https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/2955fa.pdf) push button controller  
   6. **MCU Section**  
      1. [STM32F103](https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/stm32f103cb.pdf) MCU  
      2. GPIO and I2C interface  
   7. **Output Regulators**  
      1. [AP64500SP-13](https://www.diodes.com/assets/Datasheets/AP64500.pdf) buck converter  
      2. [LM5157](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm51571-q1.pdf) boost converter  
   8. **PCB Requirements**  
      1. 2-layer PCB   
      2. FR4 material  
      3. PCB Dimensions: 107mm\*51mm   
      4. Mounting Hole :Count 4, positioned on edge corner of PCB  
      5. Mounting Hole internal diameter : 2mm  
   9. **ENIG surface finish**  
      1. 1.6mm PCB thickness

6. ## **Schematic Design Consideration**

   

![][image1]  
![][image2]

![][image3]

1. **Input Protection**  
   1. Place TVS diode near input connector  
      2. Use short GND return path  
      3. Use wide input traces  
   2. **Ideal Diode Section**  
      1. Place LM73100 close to input stage  
      2. Keep power path short  
      3. Use low ESR capacitors  
   3. **Battery Charger Section**  
      1. Follow MP2760 reference design  
      2. Place switching components close to IC  
      3. Use thermal vias under exposed pad  
      4. Separate battery sensing traces from switching traces  
   4. **MCU Power Supply**  
      1. Keep buck converter switching loop compact  
      2. Placed inductor close to regulator IC  
      3. Keep feedback trace away from noisy nodes  
   5. **MCU Section**  
      1. Added 100nF decoupling capacitor on each VDD pin  
      2. Added bulk capacitor near MCU supply  
      3. Keep crystal traces short and symmetric  
      4. Provide SWD programming header  
   6. **Load Switch Section**  
      1. Use wide copper traces for MOSFET current path  
      2. Ensure proper gate pull-up and pull-down network  
   7. **Buck Converter Section**  
      1. Minimize SW node copper area  
      2. Place input capacitor near VIN pin  
      3. Placed bootstrap capacitor close to IC  
   8. **Boost Converter Section**  
      1. Keep high current loop compact  
      2. Uses proper grounding strategy  
      3. Provided sufficient thermal copper area

7. ## **PCB Layout Consideration**

   1. **PCB Stack-Up**  
      1. Top layer for component placement,signal and power routing  
      2. Bottom layer for component placement & power routing   
   2. **Component Placement**  
      1. Placed input protection near connector  
      2. Placed charger section near battery connector  
      3. Separate switching regulators from MCU section  
      4. Keep sensitive analog traces away from power switching nodes  
   3. **Grounding Strategy**  
      1. Uses solid continuous GND plane  
      2. Avoid ground loops  
      3. Maintain low impedance return path  
   4. **Trace Width Guidelines**  
      1. 1A → 0.5mm  
      2. 2A → 1.0mm  
      3. 3A → 1.5mm  
      4. 5A → 3.0mm  
   5. **Thermal Design**  
      1. Added thermal vias under power ICs  
      2. Uses copper pours for heat spreading  
      3. Avoid thermal hotspots  
   6. **EMI/EMC Design**  
      1. Keep switching loops small  
      2. Minimize noisy SW copper area  
      3. Route I2C traces away from switching nodes  
      4. Ensure proper return current path  
   7. **PCB Requirements**  
      1. 2-layer PCB   
      2. FR4 material  
      3. PCB Dimensions: **107mm\*51mm**   
      4. Mounting Hole :**Count 4**, positioned on edge corner of PCB  
      5. Mounting Hole internal diameter : **2mm**

![][image4]

8. ## **Testing & validation**

   1. **Pre-Power Checks**  
      1. Verify component polarity  
      2. Check PCB shorts  
      3. Verify battery polarity  
      4. Inspect solder joints  
   2. **Power Validation**  
      1. Verify 12V input rail  
      2. Verify LM73100 output  
      3. Verify MP2760 charging operation  
      4. Verify 3.3V regulator output  
      5. Verify buck converter output  
      6. Verify boost converter output  
   3. **Functional Validation**  
      1. Test battery charging  
      2. Test battery backup switching  
      3. Test push-button operation  
      4. Test I2C communication  
      5. Test MCU functionality  
   4. **Reliability Validation**  
      1. Thermal testing under load  
      2. Full load stability testing  
      3. Continuous operation testing

9. ## **Risk analysis & mitigations** 

   1. **Overheating**  
      1. **Cause**: Poor thermal dissipation  
      2. **Mitigation**: Thermal vias and copper pours  
   2. **EMI Noise**  
      1. **Cause**: Large switching loops  
      2. **Mitigation**: Compact layout and proper grounding  
   3. **Reverse Polarity Damage**  
      1. **Cause**: Wrong input connection  
      2. **Mitigation**: LM73100 ideal diode protection  
   4. **Battery Damage**  
      1. **Cause**: Improper charging  
      2. **Mitigation**: MP2760 protection features  
   5. **Communication Failure**  
      1. **Cause**: I2C noise interference  
      2. **Mitigation**: Proper routing and pull-up resistors  
   6. **Voltage Spikes**  
      1. **Cause**: Input surge  
      2. **Mitigation**: SMBJ12CA TVS protection
